record.paper_title: Euclidean random matrices: solved and open problems
record.original_question: For Euclidean random matrices built from correlated random points, how can one treat the general case in which many-point correlations are present, rather than only the two-point correlations handled by existing approaches?

evidence.quote: When the points are correlated things become more difficult. Already it is difficult to study the statistical properties of correlated points and it is more difficult to study the properties of the matrices that depends on these points. Although some approaches have been developed that allow us to deal with two points correlations [6, 7], it is not evident how to treat the general case where many points correlations are present.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded region and let $\mathbf{x}_1, \dots, \mathbf{x}_N$ be random points in $V$ drawn from a joint probability distribution $P(\mathbf{x}_1, \dots, \mathbf{x}_N)$ whose marginal correlation functions
$$\rho_k(\mathbf{y}_1, \dots, \mathbf{y}_k) \;=\; \frac{N!}{(N-k)!}\int P(\mathbf{y}_1,\dots,\mathbf{y}_k,\mathbf{x}_{k+1},\dots,\mathbf{x}_N)\, d\mathbf{x}_{k+1}\cdots d\mathbf{x}_N$$
are nontrivial for arbitrary $k \geq 2$ (i.e. the points are not independent and exhibit genuine many-body correlations that do not factorize into pair correlations).

Given a deterministic measurable function $f : \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ (or $\mathbb{C}$), define the associated Euclidean random matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{N\times N}$ by
$$A_{ij} \;=\; f(\mathbf{x}_i,\mathbf{x}_j), \qquad 1 \le i,j \le N.$$

Develop a general method to compute, in the thermodynamic limit $N \to \infty$ with $N/\mathrm{vol}(V)$ fixed, the spectral properties of $A$ — in particular the limiting eigenvalue density and the resolvent $\langle (z - A)^{-1}\rangle$ — that incorporates the full hierarchy of correlation functions $\{\rho_k\}_{k\ge 2}$ of the underlying point process, rather than only the two-point correlation $\rho_2$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (2024–2026) on long-range correlated random matrices and interaction-correlated random matrices study spectral consequences of entry correlations, but a general framework for Euclidean random matrices built on point processes with arbitrary many-point correlations remains incomplete; existing analytical approaches still primarily treat the two-point (pair) correlation level.

status_evidence.title: Long-Range Correlated Random Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: A systematic understanding of how Euclidean, power-law entry correlations shape eigenvalue statistics in non-invariant, spatially embedded ensembles ... remains incomplete.
status_evidence.claim: A general theory of Euclidean random matrices with long-range/many-body entry correlations is still incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Euclidean random matrix - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: An N×N Euclidean random matrix is defined with the help of an arbitrary deterministic function f(r,r′) and of N points randomly distributed in a region V of d-dimensional Euclidean space ... strong correlations exist between different elements.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the standard definition of Euclidean random matrices and that strong entry correlations arise from the underlying point distribution.

status_evidence.title: Interaction-correlated random matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Less is known about the universal properties of the more complex random matrices with long-range correlated elements.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates that universal spectral properties under general correlated entries are not yet fully understood.
